tldr: No direct Canadian competitor product moves today, apart from BMO's quantum-computing claim. The signal comes from elsewhere: Nasdaq is preparing for 23/5 trading, Klarna is now selectable in AI-agent checkout, N26 is going upmarket with a premium account, and Brazil is in a Black Friday card-rewards push alongside a heavily traded Anthropic listing.
themes: Black Friday cashback and points offers

highlights.headline: Nasdaq has published a 23/5 Trading Information Hub, signalling near-round-the-clock US equity trading is coming.
highlights.why: Simplii's self-directed investing clients may soon expect overnight access to US stocks, so we should check platform, order-handling and support readiness.

highlights.headline: Klarna is now available as a payment option when an AI agent checks out for shoppers through Adyen Agentic.
highlights.why: Agent-driven checkout is moving from concept to live payment rails. Simplii should consider how its cards and accounts will be recognised and chosen when an AI agent makes the purchase.

highlights.headline: N26 launched Aura, its 'most exclusive' account, to pursue higher-value customers, adding to its four existing personal tiers.
highlights.why: A digital-first bank is monetising affluent users with a premium tier. This is a reference point for how Simplii might package benefits for high-balance or high-engagement clients.

highlights.headline: Anthropic's shares began trading on Nasdaq and, via a BDR, on Brazil's B3, with R$460M traded on day one, about triple SpaceX's BDR debut.
highlights.why: Retail demand for access to marquee US listings is strong, and local-market wrappers are one way to deliver it. Simplii's investing team should review how quickly clients can reach hot US IPOs.
